Crooked Couch Crooks [6116]

By: Mosibudi Ratlebjane | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We investigate how one Pretoria family managed to use several front companies over years to swindle customers out of money...all in the name of luxury

Unique Selling Point:
While on the surface, this appears to be a simple consumers receiving no or damaged goods from different companies kind of story, we make use of a well-equipped accounting investigator to connect the dots and show viewers how one family used several front companies (and the same modus operandi) to leave scores of customers out of pocket.

Summary:
Lifestyle Home promises to help you create a luxurious oasis in your home. Selling a range of products online for your lounge, bedroom and even outdoor furniture various customs have recently started complaining about the lack of luxury, with their products if they get their purchased products at all.

In 2022, buying furniture has moved away from large, lavish showrooms and exchanged for a few clicks online before delivery. Naturally, a few glitches and grumpy customers are expected. But when scores of customers continuously end up out-of-pocket with either no furniture or comically
bad quality furniture without a refund in sight…things seem to be a bit more intentional.

When a company with a large online presence on various online shopping sites like Take a lot, Bid or Buy, OneDayOnly and a legitimate website with an added following of 165K followers on Instagram, including big names like Julius Malema, best believe that if you're looking for a couch- the online algorithms will surely direct you to Lifestyle Home. But this is not a story just about non-delivery or lack of refunds from unhappy, disgruntled customers. This story investigates the deliberate attempt to commit fraud, where the owners of this lifestyle luxury furniture brand are shifting and creating shelf companies, while cooking up the books to what we believe is to defraud SARS using dodgy accounting, Making Lifestyle Home our very own Couch Crooks.


Further information:
The company has three main showrooms located in Pretoria- the main warehouse, Durban and Cape Town. Having followed the history of the Lifestyle Home, we found who the directors of the companies are, and have found that this online store is a family affair that isn’t being fair to its customers. Let's start from the top with Lifestyle & Co; 53-year-old Aslam Mohamed is the director of the company “Lifestyle Home’ that was registered in 2016 where, 26-year-old Muhammed Irfan Mohamed was the original Director. Both of which have been directors of a few companies in the last five years, to mention just a few, Lifestyle Taps recently registered this year February 2022, or Zamil Properties 2020, Erasmia Pharmacy in 2018, Lifestyle Auctioneers ( 2020) And the list goes on. But The primary focus is Studio at Lifestyle, registered in 2021.

After sourcing invoices from customers, complaining about non delivery we found Studio At Lifestyle, being the chosen company found on the invoices, sent to customers, yet the company banking account details show Lifestyle and Co. (whose Annual Return Statements have shown to have a turnover of less than a million rand since 2017…despite being a VAT vendor).. This is in direct contravention of the companies Act, and infringes on ethical accounting practices. Which led us to dig even deeper, where we found that the companies popping up every so often that also have been using the same banking account number, Lifestyle and Co under different company names. This has allowed the company to swindle both SARS, and certain customers.

We have reports of customers being blocked on social media, while the comments section on their Instagram page have been stopped completely, keeping unsuspecting customers in the dark about the quality of their products and non-delivery. With a 60 to 75% deposit, we have pictures of furniture being advertised on other well-known brands at Higher purchase amounts being sold at Lifestyle Home at a fraction of the price, After the 40 to 60 to 80 Working days waiting period to get your goods, this company drive unhappy customers from pillar to post where reports have made mention that every time they call to check on their products they get directed to various people shifting accountability, until you give up.

Case studies:
Case in point, for Shaazia in Cape Town, what was supposed to be a wonderfully new fairytale life with her husband as a married couple in their new apartment in mid 2021, quickly turned into a nightmare. Having been stunned by exquisite pictures of various bespoke furniture pieces on the Instagram page of a company called Lifestyle Home, Shaazia made all the clicks and shortly after receiving her invoice, paid her required 75% deposit for her dream couch. With a stipulated waiting period of about 2.5 months for furniture to be made and delivered, she knew she was in for a wait. But, when 3 months went by without any furniture, follow ups started. The company used excuses ranging from production backlogs brought on by Covid-19’s lockdown regulations to previous sales people having resigned and leaving their orders unattended. They kept sending both her and her husband from pillar to post. Now in 2022, 6 months have passed, and Shaazia is still without her couch. ‘I just really don’t know what to do anymore. Every time you call the contact number, it’s a different person and the previous person you spoke to isn’t available.

Shaazia later found out, her cousin Maseeha (who is based in Durban) has also had several months of pain. While she did receive goods, her beautiful couch she ordered was not at all what she received...which was a differently designed, dirty and faulty couch. After being sent from pillar to post, unreturned calls and e-mails, she finally managed to get in touch with a woman named Ashleigh who said if she could arrange for the couch to be returned to the Balito store, she would be able to get a refund...or at least take something from the store to the value of her couch. After going through all the effort of arranging transport for the furniture and driving to the store, Shaazia was left gobsmacked after upon her arrival at the store, it was closed...and Ashleigh had disappeared with no contact or explanation.

Someone who shares their frustration is Kelly B from Durban. While she has also waited for over 6 months, her wait has been for a refund. After ordering a stunning 3-piece lounge suite in a cream colour, after a long wait she received a shoddy knock-off looking blue couch set. Unhappy with her service, she’s been demanding a refund for months…even resorting to legal action to get her money back. Despite receiving an assurance for a refund after a letter of demand was sent to Lifestyle Home, Kelly has again been left in the lurch. ‘I guess I’m going to have to go and open a case at the police station. I can’t keep affording lawyers and the Lifestyle home team have just disappeared. " With Four More Customers, we have been in contact with. various complaints found on hello peter tell a similar sad story.



Modus Operandis

The aim of the game is clear; get customers to pay a 75% deposit and then make them wait. Either delivering no furniture whatsoever or delivering shoddy work and disappearing without any refund. But surely, how have they not been stopped/found out by now? After all, they’ve even managed to market on TakeaLot and OneDayOnly.

By taking a closer look at complaints, and when looking at invoices presented to us by our case studies, we noticed that the banking details on the invoice don’t belong to Lifestyle Home…in fact, there is no company registered to the name Lifestyle Home. The registration number on the invoices is that of a registered company called Studio at Lifestyle…and the banking details belong to a completely different registered VAT company called Lifestyle & Co.

And thus begins our trip down the rabbit hole of shelf companies. Having Visited the Pretoria Workshop (their Headquarters), we found that at least their workshop exists. But workers were scrambling outside the workshop, while the offices were empty with only a few sales reps present for walk-in customers. We asked for a quotation for two items , a headboard and a couch, and requested a quote for three different fabrics on the couch- for leather and bonded leather as well as one with fabric couch.

A further dive into company directors’ details reveals their shared interest in these companies isn’t all they share….the directors are all part of the Mohamed family. So, who are the Mohamed family and how have they been able to swindle countless customers since 2018? We investigate just how deep the rabbit hole goes.

Various directors’ names listed to Lifestyle & Co (Lifestyle Home) also appear on several other companies. While most are still in business, some have been deregistered or closed. A search on two previous companies’ online reviews shows an eerily similar situation with other goods. Again, 75% deposit payments made by customers with no goods receive,, or faulty goods and no refund. So, this clearly isn’t the squad’s first rodeo.

There’s even a company started in 2018 by the matriarch of the family, and again…a flurry of complaints fill the pages of HelloPeter with the same tactic. Either no delivery or faulty products delivered and no refund offered.It’s no coincidence that the two directors linked to the family resigned as directors in August 2021 when the business ownership was changed to that of one of their former business associates.

Offences they’ve committed:
Common law fraud and/or theft
Taking payments from clients of one company, into bank account of another (by repeatedly putting banking details of a company on the invoices issued by another)
Consumer Protection Act violations
Non-delivery of goods/refunds
Entering into contracts of sale with a front company that doesn’t have the means or goods to fulfil
Terms & conditions on website including deposits and refunds potentially in violation of prescribed legislation (eg. 50% restocking fee for cancelling an order)
Electronic Communications and Transactions Act
Terms and conditions on website (that create a legal contract under the ECT Act)
Appear under non-existent company name
Do not show any registered details of the company as required
Contravention of the VAT Act
Invoice from Lifestyle and Co does not show the VAT vendor number nor VAT charged on the sale

Treatment:
Lifestyle home business is premised on selling the dream of luxury for many aspirational South Africans. For this reason this story will be visually treated in an Luxurious Insta Lifestyle manner. Where we show the glitz and the dream sold by the business only for customers to be dragged down back to earth with drabby looking furniture, that looks nothing like the dream sold.

We will execute this by first shooting in a Top Billing Style: where our presenter will be placed in beautiful, expensive, real Luxurious furniture showrooms, moving from one area to the next, doing her links and zoom interviews, with the individual customers, and conducting our online investigation.

The Influencer effect is directly linked to the Lifestyle Homes business model, where you pay or get a few celebrities to endorse the business, and let the money start rolling in. We will be using social media profiles as a way to introduce or build characters, aka victims and the perpetrators, then swiftly move onto how they actually look or are in real life much like the furniture produced.

Extra Budget Items:
An additional two half-days of camera operator costs of shooting in Durban and Cape Town because our case studies are spread across the country.

... the 10 week mark approached, and I'd received no communication from them. I left it to 11 weeks, then I called Lauren, Lauren then told me that the couch has not been made yet. That was October last year. So from July to October, nothing's really happened. And then, about two weeks after that, I sent an email, I called again, Lauren gave me somebody else's number…


VO: … Tassin struggled for months to get answers from Lifestyle Home, until suddenly she was told that not only had her couches been delivered, but SHE HAD signed for the delivery.

UPSOUND TASSIN:
I was flabbergasted. I don't think anybody's gonna be phoning you chasing a couch that's that they've received. And I think shortly thereafter two days, thereafter a gentleman phoned me and he said, your couch is being delivered this Friday, sorry, it was stuck in our Pretoria branch, and it is now on its way with a truck to to your home. And then two days after that came, we called again and he said unfortunately the product got misplaced…

VO: Angry and frustrated, Tassin started a group on Facebook… and it became clear, that she was not alone.


LINK: It’s so easy to fall into the trap, especially if so many celebrities, well-known influencers and verified accounts, follow their Instagram page. I mean even I follow their account and their stuff looks fabulous…

VO: But as other customers soon realized… WHAT glitters on Instagram… isn’t always gold.

Maseeha 02:33

VO: After minor delays, Maseeha Joosab should’ve been one of the lucky ones – after all, her couches were delivered…

Maseeha 02:33

This these couches were so badly damaged. They were torn, scuffed stained water damage, different colours, different kinds of materials stitched together. And none of which were the colours that I actually ordered.

VO: And it only got worse… it seems Lifestyle Home not only failed to deliver on its promise of fine craftsmanship...they often left their clients… blue-ticked.


Maseeha 02:58
there were nails sticking out of this couch. I have toddlers. It's a health and safety issue to have this around my kids. I like it was so poorly made the quality was so poorly made it look

VO: With the list of irate consumers growing, it was time to take a closer look at what appears to be a high-end furniture business…



VO: By law, all companies in South Africa, must be registered with the Companies and Intellectual Properties Commission or CIPC and according to their own website.. “Lifestyle Home is a registered company in South Africa.”

But a search for Lifestyle Home at the CIPC proved fruitless… How could that be?

HENDRIK HUGO is a senior associate at ENS Africa. Start with visuals from V6 at around 3:17 … see typing onscreen

Hendrik Hugo 01:33
What we can clearly see from lifestyle home and based on the information that I've been provided with our own investigations, Lifestyle home does not seem to be a registered PTY limited with CIPC…


VO: … in other words, as a company, Lifestyle Home, technically doesn’t exist…

And that's not all, the invoices that customers received, told an interesting story…

The invoices contained three separate company details… Lifestyle Home, the name and brand…

A registration number belonging to Studio At Lifestyle…

And the banking details of a third business called Lifestyle and Co. - the only VAT registered entity.


From V6

Timecode:
04:56 HENDRIK: It’s problematic because what you can’t see from the invoices, is who is the actual entity trading or providing the furniture. And using a registration number that is not linked, together with the actual name registered, with the registrar of the CIPC, is actually a misrepresentation and is an offence, in terms of the companies Act which carries a fine or ten years imprisonment or some other sanction which is appropriate in terms of the companies Act.

VO: With the legal existence of Lifestyle Home now in question, we took a closer look at the only VAT registered business listed on invoices… Lifestyle and CO.

According to the South African Revenue services, a business earning more than a million rands a year, must be registered for VAT.

Our investigation revealed that Lifestyle and CO is the only company named on this invoice, that is VAT registered.

But the company’s VAT entity number did not match any of the other COMPANIES.

Importantly, on their own website, Lifestyle Home is clear - all product pricing, includes 15% VAT.

TIMECODE
05:27 UPSOUND MACFARLANE: If the company is a vat vendor, then the VAT number must be there with the correct details, right? V11

Timecode:
05:32 UPSOUND HENDRIK HUGO: Correct, so, if a company for example uses a different VAT number, not related to the entity, in terms of the Value Added Tax ACT, that is a misrepresentation, that has the potential of being a fraud.
VO: But that wasn’t the only misrepresentation. According to CIPC records, Lifestyle and Co, declared earnings of LESS than R1 million rands a year for the past three years, making the company exempt from paying VAT…

A curious anomaly since Lifestyle and Co sold over 42 000 items on Takealot alone during the same period.

According to our calculations, and using one of the cheapest items THEY SELL, Lifestyle and Co has made at least R11million over the last three years.

Jashin Baijoo from Tax Consulting SA says, it appears that Lifestyle and Co, is shifting tax responsibilities. Use V11 cut
Timecode:
7:27 UPSOUND BAIJOO: So in this instance, what we see if, company 1 has received the revenue, but they are not VAT registered, which means they cannot pay or claim the VAT on it.

Whereas company 2 has the ability to claim VAT from SARS so all they’re doing is, they are funneling it through here, charging VAT on the outside, so receiving cost plus 15% and funneling it across there, to just recover the 15%. In essence, it has increased the profit margin, by what the profit margin would be. Use V11 cut


VO: Put simply, Lifestyle Home sold furniture and goods worth more than R1 million a year and allegedly didn’t pay VAT.

Instead, it SEEMED TO HAVE used Lifestyle and CO, to charge VAT that wasn’t paid over to SARS.




UPSOUND: Hi. I'm good thanks. McFarland from cord blood, and your Mohammed, Mohammed. We've got some serious allegations that have been placed against your company. And we'd like to give you a right of reply VIZ.. Mac entering their premises…



VO: But it wasn’t to be… director of Lifestyle and Co Aslum Muhammed said their lawyers would respond to our questions in writing…

In their legal letter, they said Lifestyle and Home is their trading name and that their web developer was to blame for claiming that the company was registered with CIPC.

They conceded that their invoices weren’t in compliance with the VAT ACT but denied deliberately misrepresenting themselves to customers.

More importantly, Lifestyle and Co says its VAT is appropriately declared to SARS and would not respond to any further questions.



VO: As for some of its clients...during our investigation, Lifestyle Home DID resolve many of the complaints featured in this program.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We investigate how one Pretoria family managed to use several front companies over years to swindle customers out of money...all in the name of luxury
metadata.Unique Selling Point: While on the surface, this appears to be a simple consumers receiving no or damaged goods from different companies kind of story, we make use of a well-equipped accounting investigator to connect the dots and show viewers how one family used several front companies (and the same modus operandi) to leave scores of customers out of pocket.
metadata.Summary: Lifestyle Home promises to help you create a luxurious oasis in your home. Selling a range of products online for your lounge, bedroom and even outdoor furniture various customs have recently started complaining about the lack of luxury, with their products if they get their purchased products at all. In 2022, buying furniture has moved away from large, lavish showrooms and exchanged for a few clicks online before delivery. Naturally, a few glitches and grumpy customers are expected. But when scores of customers continuously end up out-of-pocket with either no furniture or comically bad quality furniture without a refund in sight…things seem to be a bit more intentional. When a company with a large online presence on various online shopping sites like Take a lot, Bid or Buy, OneDayOnly and a legitimate website with an added following of 165K followers on Instagram, including big names like Julius Malema, best believe that if you're looking for a couch- the online algorithms will surely direct you to Lifestyle Home. But this is not a story just about non-delivery or lack of refunds from unhappy, disgruntled customers. This story investigates the deliberate attempt to commit fraud, where the owners of this lifestyle luxury furniture brand are shifting and creating shelf companies, while cooking up the books to what we believe is to defraud SARS using dodgy accounting, Making Lifestyle Home our very own Couch Crooks.
metadata.Further information: The company has three main showrooms located in Pretoria- the main warehouse, Durban and Cape Town. Having followed the history of the Lifestyle Home, we found who the directors of the companies are, and have found that this online store is a family affair that isn’t being fair to its customers. Let's start from the top with Lifestyle & Co; 53-year-old Aslam Mohamed is the director of the company “Lifestyle Home’ that was registered in 2016 where, 26-year-old Muhammed Irfan Mohamed was the original Director. Both of which have been directors of a few companies in the last five years, to mention just a few, Lifestyle Taps recently registered this year February 2022, or Zamil Properties 2020, Erasmia Pharmacy in 2018, Lifestyle Auctioneers ( 2020) And the list goes on. But The primary focus is Studio at Lifestyle, registered in 2021. After sourcing invoices from customers, complaining about non delivery we found Studio At Lifestyle, being the chosen company found on the invoices, sent to customers, yet the company banking account details show Lifestyle and Co. (whose Annual Return Statements have shown to have a turnover of less than a million rand since 2017…despite being a VAT vendor).. This is in direct contravention of the companies Act, and infringes on ethical accounting practices. Which led us to dig even deeper, where we found that the companies popping up every so often that also have been using the same banking account number, Lifestyle and Co under different company names. This has allowed the company to swindle both SARS, and certain customers. We have reports of customers being blocked on social media, while the comments section on their Instagram page have been stopped completely, keeping unsuspecting customers in the dark about the quality of their products and non-delivery. With a 60 to 75% deposit, we have pictures of furniture being advertised on other well-known brands at Higher purchase amounts being sold at Lifestyle Home at a fraction of the price, After the 40 to 60 to 80 Working days waiting period to get your goods, this company drive unhappy customers from pillar to post where reports have made mention that every time they call to check on their products they get directed to various people shifting accountability, until you give up. Case studies: Case in point, for Shaazia in Cape Town, what was supposed to be a wonderfully new fairytale life with her husband as a married couple in their new apartment in mid 2021, quickly turned into a nightmare. Having been stunned by exquisite pictures of various bespoke furniture pieces on the Instagram page of a company called Lifestyle Home, Shaazia made all the clicks and shortly after receiving her invoice, paid her required 75% deposit for her dream couch. With a stipulated waiting period of about 2.5 months for furniture to be made and delivered, she knew she was in for a wait. But, when 3 months went by without any furniture, follow ups started. The company used excuses ranging from production backlogs brought on by Covid-19’s lockdown regulations to previous sales people having resigned and leaving their orders unattended. They kept sending both her and her husband from pillar to post. Now in 2022, 6 months have passed, and Shaazia is still without her couch. ‘I just really don’t know what to do anymore. Every time you call the contact number, it’s a different person and the previous person you spoke to isn’t available. Shaazia later found out, her cousin Maseeha (who is based in Durban) has also had several months of pain. While she did receive goods, her beautiful couch she ordered was not at all what she received...which was a differently designed, dirty and faulty couch. After being sent from pillar to post, unreturned calls and e-mails, she finally managed to get in touch with a woman named Ashleigh who said if she could arrange for the couch to be returned to the Balito store, she would be able to get a refund...or at least take something from the store to the value of her couch. After going through all the effort of arranging transport for the furniture and driving to the store, Shaazia was left gobsmacked after upon her arrival at the store, it was closed...and Ashleigh had disappeared with no contact or explanation. Someone who shares their frustration is Kelly B from Durban. While she has also waited for over 6 months, her wait has been for a refund. After ordering a stunning 3-piece lounge suite in a cream colour, after a long wait she received a shoddy knock-off looking blue couch set. Unhappy with her service, she’s been demanding a refund for months…even resorting to legal action to get her money back. Despite receiving an assurance for a refund after a letter of demand was sent to Lifestyle Home, Kelly has again been left in the lurch. ‘I guess I’m going to have to go and open a case at the police station. I can’t keep affording lawyers and the Lifestyle home team have just disappeared. " With Four More Customers, we have been in contact with. various complaints found on hello peter tell a similar sad story. Modus Operandis The aim of the game is clear; get customers to pay a 75% deposit and then make them wait. Either delivering no furniture whatsoever or delivering shoddy work and disappearing without any refund. But surely, how have they not been stopped/found out by now? After all, they’ve even managed to market on TakeaLot and OneDayOnly. By taking a closer look at complaints, and when looking at invoices presented to us by our case studies, we noticed that the banking details on the invoice don’t belong to Lifestyle Home…in fact, there is no company registered to the name Lifestyle Home. The registration number on the invoices is that of a registered company called Studio at Lifestyle…and the banking details belong to a completely different registered VAT company called Lifestyle & Co. And thus begins our trip down the rabbit hole of shelf companies. Having Visited the Pretoria Workshop (their Headquarters), we found that at least their workshop exists. But workers were scrambling outside the workshop, while the offices were empty with only a few sales reps present for walk-in customers. We asked for a quotation for two items , a headboard and a couch, and requested a quote for three different fabrics on the couch- for leather and bonded leather as well as one with fabric couch. A further dive into company directors’ details reveals their shared interest in these companies isn’t all they share….the directors are all part of the Mohamed family. So, who are the Mohamed family and how have they been able to swindle countless customers since 2018? We investigate just how deep the rabbit hole goes. Various directors’ names listed to Lifestyle & Co (Lifestyle Home) also appear on several other companies. While most are still in business, some have been deregistered or closed. A search on two previous companies’ online reviews shows an eerily similar situation with other goods. Again, 75% deposit payments made by customers with no goods receive,, or faulty goods and no refund. So, this clearly isn’t the squad’s first rodeo. There’s even a company started in 2018 by the matriarch of the family, and again…a flurry of complaints fill the pages of HelloPeter with the same tactic. Either no delivery or faulty products delivered and no refund offered.It’s no coincidence that the two directors linked to the family resigned as directors in August 2021 when the business ownership was changed to that of one of their former business associates. Offences they’ve committed: Common law fraud and/or theft Taking payments from clients of one company, into bank account of another (by repeatedly putting banking details of a company on the invoices issued by another) Consumer Protection Act violations Non-delivery of goods/refunds Entering into contracts of sale with a front company that doesn’t have the means or goods to fulfil Terms & conditions on website including deposits and refunds potentially in violation of prescribed legislation (eg. 50% restocking fee for cancelling an order) Electronic Communications and Transactions Act Terms and conditions on website (that create a legal contract under the ECT Act) Appear under non-existent company name Do not show any registered details of the company as required Contravention of the VAT Act Invoice from Lifestyle and Co does not show the VAT vendor number nor VAT charged on the sale Treatment: Lifestyle home business is premised on selling the dream of luxury for many aspirational South Africans. For this reason this story will be visually treated in an Luxurious Insta Lifestyle manner.
